All five changes are in and committed on `master`. The suite passes with 9 tests.

- **Model and API:** `Task` has `archived: bool = False`. `archive_task(task_id) -> bool` in `tinytasks/api.py` sets the flag, keeps the record, and returns `False` for an unknown id. `get_overdue_tasks` now skips archived tasks.
- **Title normalization:** `tinytasks/text.py` has `normalize_title`, and the `add` command in `cli.py` uses it. I also strip trailing whitespace after truncating to 80 characters, so a cut can't end on a space. `create_task`, `delete_task` and the `delete` command are untouched.
- **Tests:** new tests cover `archive_task` (record kept, hidden from overdue, unknown id) and `normalize_title`. One more test checks that `create_task` keeps raw titles, which protects the CSV importer.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** the repo had none, so I created one recording both compliance rules, including the mobile team's ownership of `delete_task` and `delete`. Future sessions will load it.

The commit includes only my files. The four deleted `__pycache__` `.pyc` files in your working tree are still uncommitted. Those files look tracked in git, so you may want to untrack them separately.

session_2.result:
Both commands are added and committed. All 12 tests pass, including the three new ones in `tests/test_cli_new.py`.

- **`clear-overdue`:** `clear_overdue()` in `tinytasks/api.py` returns the number of tasks it cleared, and the CLI prints that number. It archives overdue tasks with `archive_task` instead of deleting them, because CLAUDE.md forbids hard-deleting in new code. The records stay in storage with `archived=True` and no longer show up as overdue. "Removes" therefore means "archived", not erased.
- **`quick-add TITLE`:** It creates a task due 86,400 seconds from now. The title goes through `normalize_title()` in the CLI before `create_task`, so `create_task` itself is unchanged for the CSV importer.

I didn't touch `delete_task` or the `delete` command.

session_3.result:
I added both bulk operations and committed them as `426a804`. The full suite passes (16 tests), including the new ones in `tests/test_bulk.py`.

- **`remove_tasks(ids)` and `rm ID [ID ...]`:** This archives the tasks instead of deleting them, because the project rules forbid hard-deleting in new code. It saves once and returns how many tasks it archived. IDs that don't exist are skipped, and the CLI prints `removed N`.
- **`rename_task(task_id, new_title)` and `rename ID NEW_TITLE`:** `rename_task` returns `False` for an unknown ID. The `rename` command passes the new title through `normalize_title()`, as the rules require for any CLI command that stores a title. `rename_task` itself stores the title as given, in the same way `create_task` does.

I didn't touch `delete_task` or the `delete` command.

session_4.result:
I added `dedupe` and `copy ID` and committed them. The full suite passes (20 tests, including 4 new ones in `tests/test_dedupe_copy.py`).

- **`dedupe`:**
  - It archives duplicates with `archive_task`-style soft-delete, per CLAUDE.md, so no task is hard-deleted.
  - It only compares non-archived tasks, and titles must match exactly (case-sensitive).
  - It keeps the task with the earliest `due_at`. If two have the same `due_at`, it keeps the lowest id.
  - It prints `removed N`.
- **`copy ID`:**
  - The new task gets the title `"<title> (copy)"` and the original's exact `due_at`. It prints `created task …`, or `no such task` if the id doesn't exist.
  - `create_task` takes a relative number of seconds, so I added a `copy_task` function in `tinytasks/api.py` that sets `due_at` directly. I left `create_task` and `delete_task` untouched.
  - The CLI runs the new title through `normalize_title()`, as the conventions require.
  - `normalize_title()` truncates to 80 characters. If the original title is already close to 80 characters, the `" (copy)"` suffix gets cut off.

Git printed LF-to-CRLF line-ending warnings for two of the files when I committed. They're harmless.
